alt.en: A printed book page headed "Name unknown": a paragraph of text above four systems of piano music in E flat major, marked Andante.
alt.es: Una página de libro impresa con el encabezado "Name unknown": un párrafo de texto sobre cuatro sistemas de música para piano en mi bemol mayor, marcados Andante.

caption.en: Page 57 of George Petrie's collection (Dublin, 1855): the air later called the Londonderry Air, printed as "Name unknown", with his thanks to Miss J. Ross of Limavady, who sent it to him.
caption.es: La página 57 de la colección de George Petrie (Dublín, 1855): la melodía que más tarde se llamó Londonderry Air, impresa como "Name unknown" (nombre desconocido), con su agradecimiento a la señorita J. Ross, de Limavady, que se la envió.

source: The Petrie collection of the ancient music of Ireland, vol. 1 (Dublin: M. H. Gill, for the Society for the Preservation and Publication of the Melodies of Ireland, 1855), p. 57, "Name unknown"
library: Boston Public Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive petriecollection01petr, image n84 (printed page 57)
licenceEvidence: Published Dublin 1855; editor George Petrie died 1866. Public domain in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70 ended 1936). Scan of a flat page.
credit: Boston Public Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A plain printed sheet-music cover: DANNY BOY in large letters, "Song adapted from an Old Irish Air by Fred. E. Weatherly", four keys shown at the top and the Boosey & Co. imprint below, with a few handwritten notes by an owner.
alt.es: Una portada de partitura impresa, sin dibujos: DANNY BOY en letras grandes, "Song adapted from an Old Irish Air by Fred. E. Weatherly", cuatro tonalidades arriba y el sello de Boosey & Co. abajo, con algunas notas a mano de un antiguo dueño.

caption.en: The cover of a Boosey & Co. printing of Danny Boy, copyright 1913 (this copy printed in 1920 or later): it names three singers of the song and says it may be sung in public without fee or license.
caption.es: La portada de una edición de Danny Boy de Boosey & Co., con copyright de 1913 (este ejemplar se imprimió en 1920 o después): nombra a tres cantantes de la canción y dice que puede cantarse en público sin pagar derechos ni pedir licencia.

source: Danny Boy, song adapted from an Old Irish Air by Fred. E. Weatherly (New York and London: Boosey & Co., copyright 1913; this copy printed in 1920 or later, its back cover advertising a song of 1920), cover
library: Greer Music Library, Connecticut College, Historic Sheet Music Collection
callNumber: Historic Sheet Music Collection 45 (scan mirrored on the Internet Archive as sm_dannyboy, image n1)
licenceEvidence: Published New York and London, copyright 1913 (cover: "Copyright MCMXIII by Boosey & Co."); this copy printed in 1920 or later (its back cover advertises "The Barefoot Trail", "Copyright MCMXX by Boosey & Co."), a reprint of the 1913 song adding no new authorship; Weatherly died 1929; arranger not named (anonymous). Public domain in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70 ended 1999; anonymous, 70 years from publication ended 1983). Typographic cover, no figures. Scan of a flat page.

alt.en: An old bagpipe laid flat on white: a wooden bellows with leather straps, a brown leather bag, and a long dark chanter with metal keys.
alt.es: Una gaita antigua tendida sobre fondo blanco: un fuelle de madera con correas de cuero, una bolsa de cuero marrón y un puntero largo y oscuro con llaves de metal.

caption.en: Irish uilleann pipes of the 19th century, with bellows, bag and chanter. The song's "pipes" are bagpipes, though it never says which kind.
caption.es: Gaitas irlandesas uilleann del siglo XIX, con fuelle, bolsa y puntero. Las "pipes" de la canción son gaitas, aunque no dice de qué tipo.

source: Uilleann Pipe, Irish, 19th century (sheepskin, ivory, brass, wood, leather)
library: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, The Crosby Brown Collection of Musical Instruments, 1889
